title: the project registry and the two roots
acceptance: Implements design.md sections 15.1 and 15.2. config.yaml gains `default_project: firstmate-workflow` and a `projects:` map; firstmate-workflow is registered with repo `.`, github BenjaminLu/firstmate-workflow, base main, required_check ci, design design/design.md, tasks design/tasks.json. The self entry holds no copy of T-043's `project:` block; that block stays top-level until T-050 (section 15.2).

bin/fm-config.sh gains one resolver used by every later task: the project is `--project`, else FM_PROJECT, else default_project; a field lookup returns a project's value with the section 15.2 defaults for design and tasks; the project root is the engine root for repo `.` and state/projects/<name>/repo otherwise. The project is never inferred from the current directory, a git remote or a worktree.

Validation, each refused with exit 65 and a message naming the project and field: an unregistered name; a name outside [a-z0-9-] or longer than 24 characters; a repo value other than `.` or absent; a github value not shaped owner/repo; a missing base or required_check. The default project's contract resolves to T-043's top-level `project:` block, whole — every field it has, `docs` included, never a re-listed subset; a config.yaml holding both that block and a self entry `project:` is refused with exit 65.
bin/ci.sh runs its design/task-list agreement check once for every registered (design, tasks) pair and names the project on failure. No other script reads the registry yet.
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
